title: Add webapp template: .env.example files
description: Create .env.example files for both client and server templates containing placeholder environment variable keys with no real values. These serve as documentation for required configuration.
acceptanceCriteria: Server .env.example contains SMTP_HOST, SMTP_PORT, SMTP_USER, SMTP_PASS placeholders
No real values or secrets are present in either file

steps.details:
Create src/templates/webapp/server/.env.example with content:
DATABASE_URL=./data/app.db
JWT_SECRET=your-secret-key-here
PORT=3001
CLIENT_URL=http://localhost:5173
SMTP_HOST=smtp.example.com
SMTP_PORT=587
SMTP_USER=your-email@example.com
SMTP_PASS=your-smtp-password
SMTP_FROM=noreply@example.com

steps.description: Verify no real secrets are present
steps.details: Review both files to confirm all values are clearly placeholder strings (e.g., 'your-secret-key-here', 'smtp.example.com'). No real passwords, API keys, or production URLs.

technicalNotes: JWT_SECRET should be clearly labeled as requiring a strong random value in production (add a comment above it)
VITE_ prefix is required for Vite to expose env vars to the client-side code
